Q: MIME type error using django-plotly-dash in a Docker Compose stack A:

The Django runserver command may use incorrect content types for static assets. To guess content types because Django relies on the mimetypes module from the Python standard library, which itself relies on the underlying platform’s map files.

To fix this, you can force the MIME type for .js files by adding the following to your settings.py:

import mimetypes

mimetypes.add_type("application/javascript", ".js", True)

You can also try to fix your O.S. configuration. If you find improper content types for certain files, it is most likely that the platform’s map files are incorrect or need to be updated. For example:

  • On Red Hat distributions, install or update the mailcap package.

  • On Debian distributions, install or update the mime-support package.

  • On Windows O.S., edit the keys under HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT in the Windows registry.

Q: Why do my results different following along the tiny asm example? A:

I reached the same size removing the same two types of bloat: alignment padding and metadata.

nasm -f elf32 tiny.asm
gcc -m32 -s -no-pie -nostdlib -Wl,-N -Wl,--build-id=none tiny.o -o tiny_peter32
/usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld.bfd: warning: tiny_peter32 has a LOAD segment with RWX permissions

Obtained size:
-rwxrwxr-x 1 peter john 248 May 4 00:01 tiny_peter32
-rwxrwxr-x 1 peter john 248 May 4 00:00 tiny_cordes32 (main/first OP answer replication, equivalent to: “a.out” from “foo.asm”)

Alignment / Alignment+Permissions: 
-Wl,-N (OMAGIC) is more aggressive. It disables the 4KB page alignment and makes the code section writable (-Wl,--nmagic (NMAGIC) disables alignment but keeps the code read-only).
Metadata: 
-s prevents the linker from writing symbol tables (equivalent to post command-line strip).
--build-id=none removes the .note.gnu.build-id section.


I tried many options that were about to work, but I was getting all the time the same error: /usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld.bfd: tiny_peter32: error: PHDR segment not covered by LOAD segment /usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld.bfd: warning: tiny_peter32 has a LOAD segment with RWX permissions collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status

All changed when adding -no-pie that removes the structures required for that kind of executable.

Q: Getting issues writing test to run End-to-End job flow using JobOperatorTestUtils after Spring Batch 6.0.2 migration A:

Start by telling jobOperatorTestUtils what job to start:

@Autowired Job job;

jobOperatorTestUtils.setJob(job);

If that doesn't help please check configuration in the migration guide:

https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-batch/wiki/Spring-Batch-6.0-Migration-Guide#changes-related-to-enablebatchprocessing

You might need to add/tweak

@EnableBatchProcessing

Q: SQLite isn't getting installed in Docker A:

It might be that the Node image doesn't include SQLite.

To confirm, start your app with docker-compose up -d to start the container in detached mode. Use the exec command to open Bash in your container to access the container's command line, then run which sqlite3 in your container to confirm you do not have it installed:

$ docker-compose up -d
$ docker-compose exec backend /bin/bash
$ which sqlite3
$ exit

If running which sqlite3 returns no output, then you don't have SQLite installed in your container. It was working in Windows because it's installed on the OS. To fix this, you'll need to install SQLite in your Dockerfile on line 4:

RUN apt update && apt install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates

Dockerfile line 4 updated:

RUN apt update && apt install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates sqlite3
